claims.statement: Every worker event is a single flushed JSON line {v, seq, type, ...} emitted by EventWriter, which bumps seq under a threading.Lock so concurrently emitting map-phase workers keep seq monotonic and two events never interleave mid-line on stdout.

The protocol has six event types (phase, completed, prepared, refined, error, log) whose payloads are fixed by the WorkerEvent enum; the terminal events carry run results: completed (srt, txt, checkpoint, segments, filtered), prepared (engine_version), and refined (minutes).

The protocol shape is defined by four coupled files that form one commit — worker/galpi_worker/protocol.py, src-tauri/src/domain/worker.rs, src/domain/job.ts plus the Zod schemas in src/adapters/tauri-backend.ts, and the reducer in src/application/job-machine.ts — and a protocol version, event, or field must never be changed in the Python side alone.

parse_worker_event rejects malformed JSON as ProtocolError::InvalidJson and any envelope whose v differs from 1 as ProtocolError::UnsupportedVersion, so the host never half-interprets a stream from an incompatible protocol version.

The worker's stdout carries protocol only: the whole pipeline runs inside redirect_stdout(sys.stderr) so dependency prints cannot corrupt the pipe, and every abnormal exit emits exactly one error event before dying — fail("INVALID_INPUT") with exit code 2, or the catch-all fail("ENGINE_ERROR") with the exception type name and exit code 1.

run_process in adapters/outbound/process.rs is the only place the host spawns a child, and the architecture fence enforces it by failing the build when tokio::process or nix:: process primitives appear outside process.rs and its process/ submodule.

Every supervised spawn is hardened by contract: env_clear plus the explicit environment from environment.rs, null stdin, piped stdout and stderr, kill_on_drop(true), and Unix process_group(0) so signals reach the whole worker tree including uv-installed grandchildren.

ProcessSpec.worker_protocol selects how run_process treats stdout: true routes each line through parse_worker_event as protocol (used by all galpi-worker invocations), false emits each line as a Log{stream:"stdout"} event (used by the raw uv install steps in setup.rs).

read_bounded_line caps a single output line at 64 KiB (MAX_LINE_BYTES): an oversized line or non-UTF-8 output fails the run with WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR rather than buffering without bound, and a test asserts the buffer never exceeds the cap.

stderr is never protocol: run_process batches stderr lines into one Log event per 32 lines or 100 ms (also flushed when stderr closes and before early returns) so a uv pip install printing thousands of lines cannot flood the webview, while a 20-line error_tail lets a non-zero exit report PROCESS_FAILED with the most recent stderr line as detail.

Cancellation is a oneshot, not a flag: JobRegistry::cancel sends once on the channel stored with the active job (wrong id JOB_NOT_FOUND, second cancel ALREADY_CANCELLING, finished job JOB_FINISHED); run_process selects the receiver inside the read loop and around the final child.wait(), and on fire it flushes buffered stderr, SIGTERMs the process group, waits 3 seconds, SIGKILLs on timeout, always reaps the child, and returns AppError CANCELLED.

ProcessGroupGuard is the backstop that makes every non-ladder exit path safe: terminate signals the negative pid (the whole group), and while armed its Drop sends SIGKILL to the group, so a run_process future dropped mid-flight still kills the worker tree; normal completion and the cancellation ladder disarm it first.

Outbound adapters stay Tauri-blind: they emit through the JobEvents port, and the single TauriEvents instance in the inbound adapter implements that port by publishing a job-event whose payload is the domain event flattened under a camelCase jobId; composition.rs wires the same instance as both JobEvents and RecordingEvents.

The frontend validates every job-event payload against a Zod discriminated union on type mirroring domain/job.ts; toJobEvent renames the prepared event's engine_version onto the domain's engineVersion and converts unrecognized payloads into visible log events with stream "frontend" instead of throwing, because a throw inside Tauri's callback would silently swallow the event.

reduceJobEvent enforces the UI-side semantics the protocol's batching and restart behavior depend on: events from a different jobId are ignored, phase events are dropped once the status is settled, percent only moves forward within a phase (Math.max), batched log messages are split into [stream]-prefixed lines capped at 200, and completed/prepared/refined map to status completed at 100% while error maps to failed.

Cancellation is a user decision in the UI state machine: cancelJob records the notice with error null, and failJob is a no-op on an already-cancelled state, so whatever error the terminated process produced is never reported as a new failure.

The ASR context key order is a wire contract: AsrContext::into_wire_json serializes {"terms", "names", "aliases"} in that fixed order, and parse_asr_context in worker/galpi_worker/core.py reads exactly those keys — trimming entries, dropping non-string and blank entries, treating missing keys as empty lists, and raising TypeError for a non-object payload or non-array value.

The ASR context JSON travels through a private side-channel, not the protocol or the argument vector: the transcription adapter writes it with write_private_file (create_new, mode 0600, so it is never briefly world-readable), passes the path as --asr-context, and deletes the file after the run; refinement reuses the same mechanism for --background, --participants, and --glossary.

Application builds the AsrContext from trimmed assistant settings (glossary terms, participant names, spoken aliases) and AsrContext::new returns None when all three lists are empty, so no context file is created and no biasing flag is passed; application tests pin both that glossary and roster reach the port and that nothing is sent when both are empty.

The two engines consume the ASR context lists differently: WhisperX packs terms (outranking names, outranking aliases) into deduplicated first-fit hotwords under ASR_HOTWORDS_CHAR_BUDGET = 200 characters because the front of the string survives model truncation, while Qwen3 renders a freeform Korean context capped at BIAS_CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET = 500 characters.

Terminal protocol events are the only result channel and are containment-checked: the transcription adapter requires a completed event (absence is WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR) and treats an empty checkpoint string as no checkpoint, and both transcription and refinement canonicalize every worker-returned path, rejecting artifacts or minutes outside the job directory with WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR.

The frontend window mints each jobId with crypto.randomUUID() before invoking the backend, so the very first worker event already belongs to the new job and the reducer's foreign-jobId rule keeps trailing events of a just-cancelled job from leaking into the next run.

Not all protocol events originate in the worker: the host synthesizes Phase events itself (emit_phase in setup.rs) so engine/model setup progress flows through the same JobEvents channel as worker progress.

The host accepts only one terminal event per run: handle_stdout captures the first completed or refined line into ProcessResult, and a second one fails the run with WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR instead of silently overwriting the captured result.
